reading.body:
Globant files as a foreign private issuer, not a US domestic one, and its disclosure cadence is the clearest thing this data establishes.

The filing record runs from November 2025 to August 2026 and is almost entirely 6-Ks, with a single 20-F covering the year ended December 31, 2025. That is the standard pattern for a Luxembourg-domiciled company listed on the NYSE. The 20-F is the annual report, and the 6-Ks are the interim disclosures in between. A reader looking for quarterly detail in the form of 10-Qs will not find it here.

The industry classification is services, computer processing and data preparation. The revenue split in the profile text, 53.8 percent North America, 21.1 percent Latin America, 19.3 percent Europe in the fourth quarter of 2025, describes a business whose demand is concentrated in the same regions where AI data center construction is concentrated. That is a correlation in geography, not evidence of AI revenue. Nothing in this data separates AI-related work from the rest of the business.

What this data does not contain is any financial figure beyond that regional split, any customer, any contract, any headcount, and any statement about compute, power, or data center capacity. The filings are listed by date and form only. The profile text is sourced to Wikipedia and carries no numbers on cost, margin, or backlog. Anyone reading this as a measure of Globant's exposure to AI infrastructure spending is reading past what is here.

profile_text.body:
Globant is an IT and software development company founded in Buenos Aires in 2003 by Martín Migoya, Guibert Englebienne, Martín Umaran and Néstor Nocetti, and now headquartered in Luxembourg. In the fourth quarter of 2025, 53.8 percent of its revenue came from North America, 21.1 percent from Latin America and 19.3 percent from Europe.

Source: Wikipedia, Globant, retrieved 22 September 2026.
